content:
One thing that might be of interest to at least discuss is whether we want to award certificates for certain contributions to Physlib. This could be, for example, the first 10 pull requests, the first 10 reviews, or things like this. This gamifies the process a bit, and I'm not sure this is always a good idea, but it may be worth having a discussion on this.

What do people think, and does anyone have a good idea for a good way to implement this if we decide to go down this route?
The technical standard 'Open Badge 3.0' seems to be a nice practical way one could do this.

Had a mess around with this. This would allow someone to put something like the following in their CV:

Physlib Reviewer Award, Physlib, October 2026. Over the period June 2025 to September 2026, made a large contribution to reviewing pull requests to Physlib (50+ reviews). Credential: PL1:reviewer:ada-lovelace:2026-10-05:large:2025-06..2026-09:2ehCfWUJ2bjLWKoWNsxjyo97wTQ7fUEgvcQBzKCCwx51jEBRFGgseULBhAYEsocvbreUsSHQgXRQCrYgY9euEubS

And have a website like the screenshot below which automatically verifies it. Although could also be verified on any third-party service that supports Open Badge 3.0
I think this is great. Does having an open badge increase the feeling of authenticity?

Maybe not, but it does have the advantage that if "Physlib" awards the certificate to "user A", then "Physlib" does not have to store anything, and "user A" can prove that the certificate is valid using third-party scripts.

Overall I think this is great, although I agree that gamification can sometimes be negative. In this case, it is also true that currently this work is under appreciated, so this might (1) help solve this (2) also this can create a small incentive to contribute/review PRs, maybe this can also be mentioned on the website and readme

/poll Do we want reviewer badges/certificates?
Yes
No

This seems like a good implementation:
https://github.com/saiyam1814/myopenbadge

would love to get people’s thoughts on this on the poll above

Here is a draft what I have so far (very much vibe coded):

  • Home page: https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors
  • Page for a specific 'report': https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors/reports/specimen
  • Page to submit a 'report': https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors/submit

(Decided to call them reports instead of certificate or award.)

If someone wants to submit example 'reports' it would be helpful. Will delete the ones submitted now.
When we fill the github username part do we add @ or just the username
When I move to the Physlib contributors github step, I'm not able to fork the repo. Would this be an error on my side?

@Nathaneal Sajan the submission form should have been made clearer (don't add @). Hopefully I have sorted out the fork thing as well (although this is more difficult to test). would you mind checking using a Test submission which should now be an option.
Yep just opened a test, it's all working fine :)

This is what the test submission looks like:

https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors/reports/2026-10-07-test-nateabr-test-submission
I this is great for the most part, though the forking process is convoluted but seems like this is just how it works on github.
I will submit an actual one in a bit for reference
Will look into seeing if there is a better way of doing it, but yes I think this might just be a consequence of GitHub :(.
I think we can change it to GitHub issues.
@Nathaneal Sajan ok, the process of submitting should now be easier.
Yepp that's much much better
So now you can review the issue and close it if approved?

The workflow is:

  • issue is made.
  • If it looks good I can comment with 
/accept

then a bot will come along, digitally sign it using a secure key (which makes it 'official') and merge it
That is very neat - it all looks great.
Though I am confused about one thing, which is the section for just plain PRs, say for eg. someone has made 10 medium sized PRs to different areas of physlib
Good question. Maybe we need a generic "Formalization" section to cover something like this?
Yep I think that would be good, now if there is a formalization part, would we need foundational work?
Actually I do see the benefit in having foundational work

I think it might be good to have with "Foundational work" as I think the level of effort that goes into setting up good foundations is often greater than formalising based on results which already exist.
Am aligned on that point
I'm wondering if we have an "Autoformalization" section aswell or something similar for PhyslibAlpha. Though, this might be too much
Yeah I don't know about the autoformalization part, but I do think maybe including physlibalpha in the formalization section would be good
Ok, add Formalisation, and also one for Documentation.

@Nathaneal Sajan Want to submit the first proper report?

https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors/submit?section=review&name=Nathaneal%20Sajan&github=nateabr&title=Reviewed%2010%20pull%20requests%20to%20Physlib&summary=Reviewed%2010%20pull%20requests%20across%20a%20range%20of%20different%20areas,%20including%20classical%20mechanics,%20quantum%20mechanics,%20tensors%20and%20maintenance.&from=2026-07&to=2026-07&prs=1351,1348,1328,1361,1360,1358,1375,1380,1379,1401
Yep will do now!
OH you've already set this up for me - many thanks!
Done!
Yep - thought it would be nice if we could send people pre-filled forms to make it as easy as possible for them. We don't want to make more work for people :).
That's great, was also partly the reason I missed doing this yesterday :sweat_smile:

https://jstoobysmith.github.io/PhyslibContributors/reports/2026-10-08-review-nateabr-reviewed-10-pull-requests-to-physlib

This is my first verified report for reference
Thank you for setting this up @Joseph Tooby-Smith , I hope all the current contributors do confirm/make atleast one report so we have a record on this new platform :)

I have a couple more things to do here.

  1. Move the site to contributions.physlib.io
  2. Update the signing key (the one currently in use isn't so secrete as Claude made it). Will resign all certificates made with the old key once the new one is made.
  3. Add the public key to the dns of contributions.physlib.io

But from the front-end point of view it is good to go :).

I think we should prepare urls like the above for some of the main contributors :).
Yepp sounds good! Even the workflow is quite smooth now

I've now done all of the above, so the site is at:

https://contributions.physlib.io/

Still very much in beta mode. But people should feel free to start adding things!
(Also should say thanks to @Alex Zughaid for helping with the DNS side)
Can I help get prefilled forms for other collaborators? How did you set up the link?

Either you can prefill the form in and click copy a link to this form or there are instructions here:

https://contributions.physlib.io/about

int the "Links that fill in the form" which give details
Amazing, that is very thorough!
Just to confirm, would we want to submit reports as self contained work or want it as a resume of all the work a contributor has done. The section based approach would hint at the latter?

I think a bit of both.

If something falls into an obvious large self-contained work then that should be a report, but lots of people do bits and bobs all over Physlib, and that should also constitute a report I think.
Okk makes sense, so if a contributor has been contributing for a while (for eg. a maintainer), then they would have parts of a topic as a report and bits and pieces also as a report?
Something like this I think, I think it might take a while to work out exactly what we want.
Sound good, we are in the "beta" stage :)

I think a good rule might be: For a given individual we want the collection of reports that they have associated with them to roughly be what they would want to include on a CV about their contributions to Physlib. These will differ from person to person and role to role within the project. (Maybe this isn't quite right, but something along these lines...)

Yeah I think this makes sense. I was thinking something similar, for eg if we an early stage contributor who has done foundational work, lots of reviews across the board, bits and pieces of formalizations and maintenance work.

Then maybe they would make different self contained reports of foundational work topic by topic, and a full list style report of their reviews, formalizations and maintenance work seperately by section.

If you are a new contributor then you can work towards 10+ reviews or formalization PRs and submit your first report
Ofcourse approval would be at the discretion of maintainers to prevent exploits

I don't fully understand the workflow, but I think the github API only allow 60 per hour per address, so if there's more activity within an hour then the title just says Pull request #xxx if the title is filled in through the form. I don't really see why the title (optional) field is there anyway, I suggest maybe the bot summary can do this instead and auto-fill the titles, which has a higher limit for github workflows at 1000 per hour (according to Claude).
(of the 5 open items, the first two were done via the website which ran into this issue, I then asked claude to open the issues directly with the json to skip the website for the remaining ones)
